components.html:
A small contribution. A shared shelf.

  1. 01

    Make yourself at home

    Fork or clone Modshelf, then open the project in Claude Code.

  2. 02

    Let the skill do the prep

    Share your mod’s repository. The skill reads its source and creates a listing with matching artwork.

  3. 03

    Bring it to the community

    Review the changes and open a pull request. Once merged, your mod joins the shelf.

narrative.overview:
Modshelf combines warm paper, charcoal lettering, and hand-drawn objects into an approachable community catalog. The illustrations share ink contours, muted fills, and familiar desk materials; the surrounding interface gives titles, descriptions, and controls room to be read.

The same restrained controls and editorial type continue through repository contribution guidance, installation instructions, and mod details. Color marks actions and saved states; thin dividers and modest corners organize the rest. Embedded mod previews retain their native text interface inside this surrounding shelf treatment.
keyCharacteristics: Warm ivory surfaces and charcoal ink.
Newsreader headings paired with Inter controls and prose.
One family of hand-drawn ink illustrations with muted color.
Flat resting surfaces, soft hover depth, and visible keyboard focus.
A short authored bookmark settle with reduced-motion support.
Scoped native terminal text within the illustrated reading and control system.

rules.name: The Action Ink Rule
rules.body: Use rust for actionable or selected states in the surrounding Modshelf interface; keep ordinary prose in ink or muted text.

rules.name: The Terminal Color Rule
rules.body: Keep ANSI and source-specific true-color treatments within terminal demo content; retain paper, ink, and rust for the surrounding shelf controls.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Use Newsreader for headings and Inter for controls and prose; reserve monospace for commands, code, and native terminal content.

rules.name: The Terminal Cell Rule
rules.body: Preserve terminal font size and cell geometry across viewport sizes; reflow panes, controls and context around the native text.

rules.name: The Reflow Rule
rules.body: Use each surface's observed breakpoint to collapse category controls into a labeled select and stack paired content or ordered guidance; preserve readable titles and reachable actions.

rules.name: The Quiet Depth Rule
rules.body: Keep catalog surfaces flat at rest; use the existing soft shadow only for hover or the active detail layer.

dos: Do use the paper, ink, and rust roles consistently across catalog, contribution, and guidance.
Do continue the hand-drawn ink illustration family with muted fills and fully visible objects.
Do keep visible labels, rust keyboard focus, and the established phone control sizes.
Do preserve the authored bookmark state change and reduced-motion behavior.
Do preserve native terminal text geometry and ANSI states within mod previews while retaining the shelf treatment around them.
donts: Don't replace the heading and body pairing with a single display voice.
Don't add resting card shadows when a surface tone and fine border provide the existing separation.
Don't use monospace for ordinary shelf descriptions or external action labels.
Don't crop catalog illustrations into generic icon badges.
Don't replace the cc-arcade terminal with filled tiles, serif numerals, or a separate score-card toolbar.
